html:
Toyotomi Hideyoshi was the Japanese warlord who finished the reunification of Japan in 1590, the second of its three "great unifiers". Born a commoner in Owari province in 1536 or 1537, he rose to rule the whole country, something no one of such low birth had done before.

He began as a foot soldier under Oda Nobunaga and became his best general. When Nobunaga was killed by a rebel vassal in 1582, Hideyoshi beat the rebel within two weeks and took Nobunaga's place. He built Osaka Castle as his base and took the title of imperial regent, since his birth barred him from being shogun. By 1590 every daimyo had submitted, ending the long wars of Sengoku Japan.

His reforms shaped the next 250 years:

  • the sword hunt of 1588 took weapons from farmers;
  • a national land survey fixed what each field owed in rice tax;
  • an edict of 1591 froze warriors, farmers and merchants in their classes;
  • he ordered Christian missionaries out in 1587, though at first loosely.

He loved display and tea, with Sen no Rikyu as his tea master, until he ordered Rikyu's suicide in 1591. In 1592 and 1597 he sent huge armies into Korea, aiming at Ming China. The Imjin War stalled against the Korean navy of Yi Sun-sin and Ming armies, and the troops came home after he died in 1598. His ally Tokugawa Ieyasu then took power and destroyed the Toyotomi family in 1615.
